question: Two addicts cannot resist the drug. One hates his craving; one welcomes it. On Frankfurt's view, who can be responsible for taking it?
answer: The one who welcomes it. In his 1971 paper Frankfurt calls the unwilling addict a helpless bystander to a desire he rejects. The willing addict could not resist either, but he endorses the craving and makes it his own, so he may be morally responsible. Same craving, same drug: only one is on its side.
move: Ask not only what someone wants, but whether they want to want it.
ask: Which habit of mine do I act on without ever asking whether I want to want it?
trap: Assuming nobody answers for an act they could not have resisted.
reference: Frankfurt, Freedom of the Will and the Concept of a Person, Journal of Philosophy 68 (1), 1971
